questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following is an INCORRECT match?
options: Electron Gain enthalpy - $F \lt  Cl \gt  Br \gt  I$
First Ionization Enthalpies - $Na \lt  Mg \gt  Al \lt  Si$
questions.solution:
Metallic character increases down a group and decreases from left to right across a period.

Potassium ($K$) is an alkali metal in group 1 and period 4, making it the most metallic among the given elements. Boron ($B$) is a metalloid in group 13 and period 2, making it the least metallic.

Magnesium ($Mg$) and Aluminum ($Al$) belong to period 3. Since $Mg$ is in group 2 and $Al$ is in group 13, $Mg$ is more metallic than $Al$.

The correct order of metallic character is $K \gt Mg \gt Al \gt B$.

The given order $Al \gt Mg \gt B \gt K$ is incorrect.

Answer: Metallic character - $Al \gt Mg \gt B \gt K$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Arrange the following ions in the decreasing order of their ionic radii: $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}, \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}, \mathrm{S}^{2-}, \mathrm{K}^{+}$
questions.solution:
The given ions are $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$, $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$, and $\mathrm{K}^{+}$.

First, determine the number of electrons in each ion:
$\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ has $16 + 2 = 18$ electrons.
$\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ has $17 + 1 = 18$ electrons.
$\mathrm{K}^{+}$ has $19 - 1 = 18$ electrons.
$\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ has $20 - 2 = 18$ electrons.

All these ions are isoelectronic, meaning they have the same number of electrons ($18$).

For isoelectronic species, the ionic radius decreases as the nuclear charge (atomic number, $Z$) increases, because a higher nuclear charge pulls the same number of electrons more strongly towards the nucleus.

The atomic numbers are:
$\mathrm{S} (Z = 16)$
$\mathrm{Cl} (Z = 17)$
$\mathrm{K} (Z = 19)$
$\mathrm{Ca} (Z = 20)$

Arranging them in decreasing order of ionic radii based on increasing atomic number:
$\mathrm{S}^{2-} (Z=16) \gt \mathrm{Cl}^{-} (Z=17) \gt \mathrm{K}^{+} (Z=19) \gt \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} (Z=20)$.

Answer: $\mathrm{S}^{2-}\gt \mathrm{Cl}^{-}\gt \mathrm{K}^{+}\gt \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
The first ionisation enthalpy of Al in $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ is:
[Given the first ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{Mg}$ and Si in $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ are 497, 738 and 787 respectively]
questions.solution:
The first ionisation enthalpy values for the elements in the third period are as follows: Na (497), Mg (738), Al, and Si (787).

The general trend for ionisation enthalpy across a period is an increase due to the increase in effective nuclear charge. However, there are exceptions due to the stability of electronic configurations.

The electronic configuration of Mg is $[Ne] 3s^2$, which is a fully filled s-orbital, making it exceptionally stable. Consequently, the first ionisation enthalpy of Mg is higher than that of Al, which has the configuration $[Ne] 3s^2 3p^1$.

The electronic configuration of Al is $[Ne] 3s^2 3p^1$. Removing the $3p^1$ electron is easier than removing a $3s^2$ electron from Mg. Thus, the ionisation enthalpy of Al must be lower than that of Mg (738) but higher than that of Na (497).

Among the given options, 578 is the only value that lies between 497 and 738.

Answer: 578

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The first electron gain enthalpy of oxygen is $-141 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$, its second electron gain enthalpy is:
options: Less negative value than the first
Maximum negative value than the first
Same value as that of the first
questions.solution:
The first electron gain enthalpy of oxygen is exothermic because energy is released when an electron is added to a neutral oxygen atom to form an $O^{-}$ ion, resulting in a stable configuration. The process is represented as: $O(g) + e^{-} \rightarrow O^{-}(g)$, $\Delta H = -141 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

The second electron gain enthalpy involves adding an electron to a negatively charged $O^{-}$ ion to form an $O^{2-}$ ion: $O^{-}(g) + e^{-} \rightarrow O^{2-}(g)$.

Since both the incoming electron and the $O^{-}$ ion are negatively charged, there is a strong electrostatic repulsion between them. To overcome this repulsion and force the electron into the ion, energy must be supplied to the system.

Therefore, the second electron gain enthalpy is endothermic, which corresponds to a positive value.

Answer: A positive value

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
Choose the pair of elements $[(A)$ to $(F)]$ which:
(i) belong to the Chalcogen family
(ii) form monovalent oxides which give alkalies in aqueous solution
(iii) form stable monovalent anions

$(A)1 s^2 2 s^2 2 p^6 3 s^2 3 p^6 4 s^1  \quad (B) 1 s^2 2 s^2 2 p^5  \quad (C) 1 s^2 2 s^2 2 p^6 3 s^1  \quad 
(D) 1 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{p}^6 3 \mathrm{~s}^2 3 \mathrm{p}^5  \quad (E) 1 s^2 2 s^2 2 p^6 3 s^2 3 p^4  \quad (F) 1 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{p}^4$
questions.solution:
Identifying each element by valence configuration:

A ($4s^1$) → Group 1 (Alkali metal)
B ($2s^22p^5$) → Group 17 (Halogen)
C ($3s^1$) → Group 1 (Alkali metal)
D ($3s^23p^5$) → Group 17 (Halogen)
E ($3s^23p^4$) → Group 16 (Chalcogen)
F ($2p^4$) → Group 16 (Chalcogen)

(i) Chalcogen family (Group 16): E and F

(ii) Monovalent oxides giving alkalies (Group 1, $ns^1$): A and C (form $Na_2O$, $K_2O$ type oxides → alkaline solution)

(iii) Stable monovalent anions (Group 17, need 1 electron): B and D

Answer: (i) E&F, (ii) A&C, (iii) B&D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are true about the diagonal relationship of Be and Al ?
(i) Both react with NaOH to liberate hydrogen.
(ii) Their oxides are basic.
(iii) They are made passive by nitric acid.
(iv) Their carbides give acetylene on treatment with water.
questions.solution:
Statement given in (i) and (iii) are correct, while in (ii) and (iv) are incorrect.
BeO and $\mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ are amphoteric. These react with acid as well as alkalines to given corresponding salts.
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{BeO}+2 \mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{BeCl}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ \\ & \mathrm{BeO}+2 \mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{BeO}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ \\ & \mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+6 \mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{AlCl}_3+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ \\ & \mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+2 \mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaAlO}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ \end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{Be}_2 \mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{Al}_4 \mathrm{C}_3$ give methane on treatment with water.
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{Be}_2 \mathrm{C}+4 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_2+\mathrm{CH}_4 \\ \\ & \mathrm{Al}_4 \mathrm{C}_3+12 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH})_3+3 \mathrm{CH}_4 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following species has lowest ionisation enthalpy?
questions.solution:
During addition of electron to $\mathrm{O}_2$ to form $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$, the additional $\pi$-molecular electron is added to the less stable antibonding orbital.
Therefore, it is easier to remove an electron from $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$ ion to form a neutral $\mathrm{O}_2$ molecule.
Thus ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$is lowest.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Among the following, which is not according to the property indicated against it?
options: $\mathrm{I}\lt \mathrm{Br}\lt \mathrm{F}\lt \mathrm{Cl} \text { [Increasing Elecrtron Gain Enthalpy with negative sign] }$
questions.solution:
Option (1): The electron gain enthalpy (magnitude) for halogens follows the order $\mathrm{I} \lt \mathrm{Br} \lt \mathrm{F} \lt \mathrm{Cl}$. Due to the small size of fluorine, interelectronic repulsions are high, making $\mathrm{Cl}$ have a more negative electron gain enthalpy than $\mathrm{F}$. This is correct.

Option (2): The first ionization enthalpy generally increases across a period. However, $\mathrm{N}$ has a stable half-filled $2p^3$ configuration, making its ionization enthalpy higher than that of $\mathrm{O}$. The correct order is $\mathrm{B} \lt \mathrm{C} \lt \mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{N}$. Thus, the given statement is incorrect.

Option (3): For isoelectronic species, the ionic size increases as the nuclear charge decreases. The nuclear charges are $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+} (12)$, $\mathrm{Na}^{+} (11)$, $\mathrm{F}^{-} (9)$, and $\mathrm{O}^{2-} (8)$. The order $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+} \lt \mathrm{Na}^{+} \lt \mathrm{F}^{-} \lt \mathrm{O}^{2-}$ is correct.

Option (4): Metallic radii increase down a group due to the addition of new shells. The order $\mathrm{Na} \lt \mathrm{K} \lt \mathrm{Rb} \lt \mathrm{Cs}$ is correct.

Answer: $\mathrm{B}\lt \mathrm{C}\lt \mathrm{N}\lt \mathrm{O} \text { [Increasing First Ionisation Enthalpy] }$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: With reference to Pauling's Electronegativity scale, which one of the following options shows the correct order of electronegativity values of elements?
questions.solution:
The Pauling electronegativity values for the elements are as follows:

Nitrogen (N) = 3.04, Sulfur (S) = 2.58, Phosphorus (P) = 2.19. Thus, N > S > P is correct.

Sodium (Na) = 0.93, Cesium (Cs) = 0.79, Potassium (K) = 0.82. The order Na > K > Cs is correct, so Na > Cs > K is incorrect.

Magnesium (Mg) = 1.31, Aluminum (Al) = 1.61, Silicon (Si) = 1.90. The order Mg < Al < Si is correct, so Mg > Al > Si is incorrect.

Boron (B) = 2.04, Carbon (C) = 2.55, Aluminum (Al) = 1.61. The order C > B > Al is correct, so B > C > Al is incorrect.

Answer: $\mathrm{N}\gt \mathrm{S}\gt \mathrm{P}$

questions.q: The correct decreasing order of negative electron gain enthalpy for $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{Ca}, \mathrm{Al}, \mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{O}$ is
questions.solution:
Electron gain enthalpy becomes less negative as we move down in a group white it becomes more negative along the period.
$\therefore$ Correct order is
$\mathrm{F}\gt \mathrm{O}\gt \mathrm{C}\gt \mathrm{Al}\gt \mathrm{Ca}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
The group number of the element in the periodic table with the electronic configuration $(\mathrm{n}-1) \mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{~ns}^2$.
For $n=4$ is:
questions.solution:
The given electronic configuration is $(n-1)d^2 ns^2$.

For $n=4$, the configuration becomes $(4-1)d^2 4s^2$, which is $3d^2 4s^2$.

This element is Titanium (Ti), which has an atomic number of 22.

For transition elements (d-block elements), the group number is determined by the sum of electrons in the $(n-1)d$ subshell and the $ns$ subshell.

Group number = (number of electrons in $(n-1)d$) + (number of electrons in $ns$).

Group number = $2 + 2 = 4$.

Therefore, the element belongs to Group 4.

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The correct decreasing order of negative electron gain enthalpy for $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{Ca}, \mathrm{Al}, \mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{O}$ is
questions.solution:
The electron gain enthalpy is the energy released when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous atom. Generally, it becomes more negative (higher magnitude) across a period from left to right and decreases down a group.

The elements given are $\mathrm{F}$ (Group 17, Period 2), $\mathrm{O}$ (Group 16, Period 2), $\mathrm{C}$ (Group 14, Period 2), $\mathrm{Al}$ (Group 13, Period 3), and $\mathrm{Ca}$ (Group 2, Period 4).

Comparing the magnitudes of electron gain enthalpy:
1. $\mathrm{F}$ has the highest negative electron gain enthalpy among these due to its small size and high effective nuclear charge, although it is slightly less than $\mathrm{Cl}$ due to inter-electronic repulsion.
2. $\mathrm{O}$ follows $\mathrm{F}$ in the same period.
3. $\mathrm{C}$ has a lower negative electron gain enthalpy than $\mathrm{O}$.
4. $\mathrm{Al}$ is a metal with a low tendency to gain electrons, but it is more electronegative than $\mathrm{Ca}$.
5. $\mathrm{Ca}$ is an alkaline earth metal with a stable $ns^2$ configuration, making its electron gain enthalpy very low (near zero or positive).

The order of magnitude of negative electron gain enthalpy is $\mathrm{F} \gt \mathrm{O} \gt \mathrm{C} \gt \mathrm{Al} \gt \mathrm{Ca}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{F}\gt \mathrm{O}\gt \mathrm{C}\gt \mathrm{Al}\gt \mathrm{Ca}$

questions.q: In the following, the element with the highest ionisation energy is
questions.solution:
The element [Ne] $3 s^{2} 3 p^{3}$ have half-filled $p$-orbital.
As a result, it is more stable.
$\therefore$ The ionisation energy is highest for this element.

questions.solution: The correct order in which first ionisation potential (IP) increases is $\mathrm{K}, \mathrm{Na}$, Be. On going down the group IP decreases while on going left to right IP increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Atomic numbers of vanadium, chromium, nickel and iron are $23,24,28$ and 26 respectively. Which one of these is expected to have the highest second ionisation enthalpy?
questions.solution: Second ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{Cr}$ is highest because after the removal of 1st electron, Cr acquires a stable half-filled $d^{5}$ configuration thus, removal of 2 nd electron is very difficult.

questions.q: The atomic number of the element with highest ionisation energy among the following is
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration is
(a) $Z=16: 1 s^{2} 2 s^{2} 2 p^{6} 3 s^{2} 3 p^{4}$
(b) $Z=14: 1 s^{2} 2 s^{2} 2 p^{6} 3 s^{2} 3 p^{2}$
(c) $Z=13: 1 s^{2} 2 s^{2} 2 p^{6} 3 s^{2} 3 p^{1}$
(d) $Z=15: 1 s^{2} 2 s^{2} 2 p^{6} 3 s^{2} 3 p^{3}\because$ For $Z=15, p$-orbital has stable half-filled configuration.
$\therefore$ It will have highest ionisation energy.
